html:
People ask "what should deep cleaning cost?" before anything else, and it is the right question. The answer in Greer, SC is a set of factors rather than a number, because the work behind the name can be very different from house to house. Here is how the hours stack up.

Start with the base time

The base time comes from home size: square feet and the number of rooms. Think of it as how long a team would need if the home were in decent shape with no extras. A compact townhome near Downtown Greer sits at the low end, a large two-story near the BMW plant at the high end.

Then condition, the biggest swing

This is where two similar houses split. A home professionally cleaned six months ago needs a lot less than one that has not been cleaned in years. Heavy build-up takes longer to remove: grease on cabinet fronts, soap scum, dust packed on fan blades. We see it most in kitchens and bathrooms. A deep cleaning is designed to deal with exactly that, but it takes the time it takes.

Bathrooms and hard water

Bathrooms are the slowest work in a deep clean. Grout lines get scrubbed, hard water spots on glass and chrome need dwell time, and the area behind and around the toilet base gets attention. A house with four bathrooms is a very different job from a house with two, even at the same square footage.

Add-ons that increase time

  • Inside the oven
  • Inside the fridge
  • Inside cabinets and drawers
  • Interior windows and blinds beyond the standard sills and tracks
  • Pet stains and heavy pet hair

Each of these is optional. They are listed in the estimate so you can pick what is worth it for you.

Access and clutter

Clear rooms clean faster. If the team has to move stacks of paper, toys and dishes to reach a counter, the clock keeps running. Spending 20 minutes picking up before the visit often saves more than that in cleaning time.

What you get for the price

A deep cleaning in Greer includes everything in a regular visit plus baseboards and door frames hand-wiped, cabinet fronts and handles degreased, grout scrubbed in the kitchen and bathrooms, ceiling fan blades, vents and light fixtures dusted, window sills, tracks and blinds cleaned, and appliance exteriors with the range hood and backsplash. See the full list on our deep cleaning service page.

Is it worth the price?

For many homes, it is the reset that makes everything else easier. After a deep clean, a regular maid service visit is faster and costs less to maintain. Allergy sufferers also notice the difference when dust is removed rather than moved. We have seen homeowners in Greer use a deep clean before the holidays or before listing a home, and the same logic applies to spring pollen season.

How to keep the price down without losing quality

  1. Clear counters and floors before the visit
  2. Pick only the add-ons you will use
  3. Plan a regular schedule after the deep clean, so you do not need another one soon
  4. Tell us about problem areas ahead of time
  5. Book early, because busy seasons fill up

How long it takes depends on the same factors, and we share the time estimate at the visit. Booking this week is often possible. How timing affects the price

Schedule matters, too. Spring and the weeks before Thanksgiving and Christmas fill up quickly in Greer, so the dates available to you may be fewer, and a flexible day of the week gives us more room to plan a team that fits your home. Asking for a specific weekend with short notice can limit options. If you are cleaning ahead of a move or a sale, build in a few days so the result is not rushed.

Finally, think about what happens after the visit. A deep clean paired with a regular schedule keeps the home near the same standard, so you do not pay for another large reset a few months later. That is usually the best use of the first visit, and it is something we can plan with you at the estimate.
